title: Interaction Compatibility Covenant: PRD for Unified Hosted Endpoint Family and Gatekeeper Rollout
creator: Maya Rivera
description:
Purpose: Define a product requirements document (PRD) and gated launch checklist for a family of hosted endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) under a single compatibility contract (the 'Interaction Compatibility Covenant').

Context: We are consolidating multiple hosted surfaces into one coherent family so integrators can expect consistent behavior, graded degration, and predictable unit economics. This PRD codifies non-functional expectations (latency SLOs, cost bands), deterministic vs probabilistic guarantees, behavioral regression thresholds, and the staged rollout (internal alpha -> invited beta -> GA).

Scope: Includes API surface contracts, model variant mapping rules, fallback routing policies, per-endpoint acceptance tests, telemetry & eval gating, SDK/CLI updates, and launch playbook.

Out of scope: New model training, on-prem install packaging, enterprise billing changes.

Success metrics: 1) GA adoption: 75% of new hosted integration signups use unified endpoints within 3 months. 2) Observability: <0.5% quality-regression alerts on eval suites during canary. 3) Performance: 95th percentile L2 latency within configured lane targets. 4) Cost: median per-token cost reduction >=5% after default batching and cache profiles applied.
acceptance_criteria: API contract: single /v1/interaction endpoint documented with parameter mappings for chat, completions, embeddings, rerank and a clear 'mode' field; backwards-compatible aliases must be supported for existing endpoints (deprecated after 6 months).

Behavioral determinism: when caller requests deterministic=true on generation lanes, response variance must be within documented token-level entropy bounds on 98% of eval prompts (eval harness reference: eval-unified-2026).
Latency SLOs: for P99 traffic in Fast lane: <= 300ms for up to 512 tokens generated; for Standard lane P95 <= 700ms.
Cost profiles: default 'Balanced' lane should apply batching/quantization profiles to achieve >=5% unit cost savings relative to baseline for the canonical workloads in perf-suite-2026.
Quality gates: embedding similarity drift < 1.5% on baseline embedding dataset; rerank NDCG drop < 0.8% across top-10. Failing thresholds block rollout.
Observability: per-model/per-lane dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and 'interaction-sla' alerting rule created and tested in prod-sandbox.
Rollout controls: canary must support traffic slicing by tenant, region, and lane; automatic rollback triggers on defined SLO/quality thresholds.
SDKs & docs: client SDKs (python/js) updated and published; Quickstart + migration guide and compatibility matrix available in Confluence.

Security & compliance: KMS integration validated for request-level keys; audit log entries for each endpoint invocation logged to customer-managed S3 for Private deployments as per security checklist.
launch_checklist: Finalize API surface spec and update OpenAPI/JSON schema (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pulls/6942).
Complete deterministic-seed behavior design and add unit/integration tests (ENG PR referenced above).
Publish migration guide and deprecation timeline to docs (Confluence: /display/RED/Interaction+Compatibility+Covenant).
Wire up eval harness and schedule full canary run against grade-A customers; capture baseline metrics (dashboard: grafana/redwood/eval-unified-2026).
Create and validate canary traffic slices (tenant, region, lane) in SRE runbook; dry-run rollbacks.
SDK release: python v1.8.0 and js v2.3.0 with compatibility flags.
Operational readiness: create runbook, oncall rotations, and run a game day for rollback scenario.
Security review: complete privacy/KMS signoff and record findings (Security doc link in links).
GA sign-off: PM, Eng, SRE, Design, Legal and Security approvals captured in ticket.
decisions: Default to a single unified /v1/interaction entrypoint with a 'mode' selector vs multiple endpoints to reduce cognitive surface for integrators.
Support both deterministic=true (seed-based) and stochastic sampling; deterministic mode will be ESB-backed and routed to pinned model variants to reduce variance.
Adopt graded degradation policies: Prefer cheaper quantized model variants when under capacity constraints but enforce a quality delta threshold to avoid unacceptable regressions.
Canary gating will combine SLO-based metrics and eval-harness signal; both must pass for automatic traffic ramp.
tradeoffs: Single endpoint reduces surface area but adds complexity to server-side routing logic and backwards-compatibility handling for legacy clients.
Enforcing deterministic guarantees increases caching and KV pressure; this requires extra memory and may increase tail latency for some workloads.
Using quantized fallback variants reduces cost but risks subtle quality shifts for few prompts; mitigations include per-tenant allowed-variance toggles.
